verdict.rationale: ROS 2 ships its own credential mechanism via sros2/DDS-Security. Users create a keystore (`ros2 security create_keystore`) and security enclaves, each of which "encapsulates a single policy for protecting ROS communications." Enclaves can be mapped to processes, users or devices, so an agent node could be issued its own scoped, authenticated identity. The evidence describes this only generically as graph-participant security, not as least-privilege API credentials for agents. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of fine-grained per-topic/service permission scoping, any agent-oriented credential issuance or revocation flow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
